newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: POLYGRAM Q1 NET SEEN RISING MODERATELY.
newsitem.headline: POLYGRAM Q1 NET SEEN RISING MODERATELY.

text.p: Dutch music and entertainment group PolyGram NV is expected to report a small rise in first quarter profits boosted by currency gains, said analysts ahead of its first ever quarterly results announcement next Tuesday.
Analysts' net profit forecasts for the first quarter of 1997 ranged up to 135 million guilders, although some pointed to a "moderate" rise on the year ago period, without giving detail.

A spokeswoman for PolyGram said according to unaudited figures the company made 124 million guilders net in the first quarter of 1996, on turnover of 2.03 billion guilders and with income from operations of 192 million.

"They will definitely benefit from currency effects this year, and in the first quarter as well. With the current position of the guilder it will have a substantial impact on earnings growth," said Wijnand Heineken, analyst at Labouchere.
"PolyGram is benefiting from the strength of the dollar and the strength of the British pound and that's a material influence," said Andre Moons of ING Barings.
He is going for a first quarter net profit of 135 million guilders, with the performance in Europe also helped by the impact of local artists such as Andrea Bocelli of Italy.

Analysts said PolyGram, which announced a fall in 1996 net income to 722 million guilders from 741 million, before a $90 million extraordinary restructuring charge in a tough music retail climate, should feel the benefit from the March 1997 release of the long-awaited new album from Irish pop band U2.
The album, originally expected in 1996, has gathered positive reviews and high chart placings, say analysts.

"My impression from last year was the first quarter was a bit weak on the music side," said Heineken. "This first quarter could be stronger because the U2 album was delayed." The music arm of PolyGram generated 84 percent of group sales in 1996.
Sales from two albums from veteran singing trio The Bee Gees could also help results in the first quarter, analysts say.
"We're going for something marginally up on what they would have reported a year ago if they had reported," said one London-based analyst who declined to be named.
"It's quite possible I'm being on the conservative side because there are a number of releases out there which I believe have done quite well," he added.
"In the first quarter you tend to get momentum that you've built up over the Christmas period still running through a bit and you'll see the impact of U2 in the first quarter."

The company has reported its PolyGram Filmed Entertainment (PFE) unit made a two million guilder operating profit in the second half of 1996, with full year operating losses of 35 million guilders, down from 68 million in 1995.
PolyGram president and chief executive Alain Levy has said the unit would not make a profit in 1997.
PolyGram is listed in Amsterdam and New York with many of its senior executives based in London. Dutch electronics giant Philips Electronics NV holds a 75 percent stake.
